acceptance_criteria: New documented variant `HoleKind::Countersink { diameter: f64, csk_diameter: f64, csk_angle: f64 }`. `csk_angle` is the included cone angle in radians (e.g. π/2 for 90°). The cone runs from `csk_diameter` at `at.origin` down to `diameter`, so its depth along the drill direction is `(csk_diameter − diameter) / 2 / tan(csk_angle / 2)`. Blind depth is still measured from `at.origin` to the flat hole bottom.

`OcctKernel::hole` cuts the countersink for `Blind` and `ThroughAll`, and the existing `Simple` and `Counterbore` tests still pass unchanged. Any new shim function is `noexcept`, catches C++ exceptions, and the result is rejected when `BRepCheck_Analyzer` finds it invalid.

Tests (behind `occt`), box `make_box((0, 0, 0), (40, 30, 20))`, volumes within a relative 1e-6, boxes within 1e-6. Countersink Ø6 / Ø12 at 90° (cone depth 3, cone volume 63π): through all, at (20, 15, 20) along −Z: volume 24000 − 216π ≈ 23321.4160; 8 faces; bounding box unchanged. blind 10, same axis: volume 24000 − 126π ≈ 23604.1593; 9 faces. blind 10 on a side face, at (0, 15, 10) along +X: volume ≈ 23604.1593; the hole bottom face's box is (10, 12, 7)–(10, 18, 13). the input solid is unchanged (volume 24000, 6 faces).

Errors, each with a test and never a panic, all `InvalidInput` checked before the backend (kernel-free tests without `occt` where possible): `diameter` or `csk_diameter` zero, negative or not finite; `csk_diameter` ≤ `diameter`; `csk_angle` not finite or not strictly between 0 and π; a blind depth ≤ the cone depth.
No new dependencies. Every new `unsafe` block is in `ffi` and documented; any new doc comment for the cone construction cites its source (OCCT reference documentation of the calls used).
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
